title: Historical disciplinary-register normalization and safe import contract
summary: Deterministic analysis of the 17 supplied fiscal disciplinary workbooks establishes the normalization rules needed for safe migration: 1,193 populated event rows, four header layouts, inconsistent department/job-title/type/reason vocabularies, no exact duplicate rows, and legitimate multi-record same-person/same-date groups.

claims.claim: The supplied fiscal registers contain 1,193 populated event rows across the historical coverage analyzed; the 2025-2026 workbook contributes zero events because it is an empty template.

Four distinct fiscal-register header layouts occur: the 2008-2009 ORIGIN/EEO-1 layout; a 2009-2014 RACE/EE0-1 layout; a 2014-forward layout adding VET and IWD; and a trailing-blank-column variant. The source frequently spells the EEO field as EE0-1 with a zero.

Department values are not normalized: Operations, Opr and Opr. all occur; Adm and Adm. both occur; Café has spelling/punctuation variants; Maintenance occurs separately; one event has no department value.

Job-title values contain meaningful and cosmetic variants, including Driver/PT Driver/P.T. Driver/Temp. Driver/Job Shop Driver; Area Manager/Area Mgr; Data Entry/Res/DE/Reserv; Garage Attendant misspellings/abbreviations; Café Assistant variants; Accounts Receivable variants; Receptionist/Clerical-Recep and other role labels.

evidence.note: Alias examples only; do not collapse semantically distinct roles without role-history validation.

claims.claim: Thirteen populated fiscal rows have a blank TYPE value, while historical type labels also vary by spelling/roman-vs-arabic numerals and include non-disciplinary labels such as Incident.
The fiscal registers contain 276 distinct free-text REASON strings, confirming that reason is a narrative/compound field rather than a controlled single-value taxonomy.

No exact duplicate event rows were found across the fiscal registers, but 24 same-person/same-date groups contain two or three distinct records; 13 of those groups also share the same reason text. Therefore employee+date and employee+date+reason are not safe unique keys.

evidence.note: Aggregate duplicate-key result only; employee identities excluded.

claims.claim: The safe migration design should preserve every source row with a stable source-row identity and store normalized aliases/categories alongside—not instead of—the raw source values.

trigger: Legacy disciplinary/AAP spreadsheets are imported or migrated.
prerequisites: Restricted processing environment for employee/protected-class data.
Source workbook hash and schema/year identified.
steps: Assign each source workbook a hash/version and each populated source row a stable source-row ID.
Detect the workbook schema/header variant instead of assuming fixed column positions.
Normalize department/job-title/type/reason into separate derived fields while preserving raw values.
Classify event type explicitly, including discipline versus vehicle incident.
Do not deduplicate on person/date/reason; only exact-row/hash evidence may support duplicate treatment, and even exact repeats require provenance review.
Validate blank/unknown fields and report them rather than silently defaulting.
Retain source-to-normalized mappings and confidence for audit/replay.
decisions: Exact duplicate versus multiple legitimate records on the same date.
controls: Never overwrite raw historical values with normalized values.
Never use employee+date or employee+date+reason as the primary key.
Header spelling and position must be schema-detected.
Free-text reasons may map to multiple derived categories.
Role/title normalization must respect effective-dated job history.
unresolved_questions: What stable event ID should be used for historical records that lack a native identifier?
Which job-title aliases should map to one canonical role versus remain distinct historical positions?
How should WW1-WW9/roman-numeral warning labels be normalized once their historical semantics are validated?
automation_candidates: Build year/schema adapters with regression fixtures from every header layout.
Generate stable event IDs from source hash + sheet + source row number.
Maintain alias tables for department/title/type with effective dates and human-review status.
Add import tests proving same-date multi-record events survive normalization unchanged.

provenance.notes: All row-level processing occurred locally; identities/protected values excluded from durable generalized knowledge.
